import android.content.Context
import android.content.SharedPreferences
import org.json.JSONObject

class DayStore(context: Context) {

    private val prefs: SharedPreferences =
        context.getSharedPreferences("ruh_days", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)

    init {
        val legacy = prefs.getString("rapidapi_key", null)
        if (!legacy.isNullOrBlank() && prefs.getString("key_aerodatabox", "")?.isBlank() != false) {
            prefs.edit().putString("key_aerodatabox", legacy.trim()).apply()
        }
    }

    fun activeSource(): String =
        prefs.getString("active_source", Sources.AERODATABOX) ?: Sources.AERODATABOX

    fun setActiveSource(id: String) {
        prefs.edit().putString("active_source", id).apply()
    }

    fun keyFor(src: String): String =
        prefs.getString("key_$src", "") ?: ""

    fun setKeyFor(src: String, key: String) {
        prefs.edit().putString("key_$src", key.trim()).apply()
    }

    fun getKey(): String = keyFor(activeSource())

    fun setKey(key: String) = setKeyFor(activeSource(), key)

    fun lastApiOk(): Boolean = prefs.getBoolean("api_ok", true)
    fun lastApiMsg(): String = prefs.getString("api_msg", "") ?: ""
    fun setLastApi(ok: Boolean, msg: String) {
        prefs.edit().putBoolean("api_ok", ok).putString("api_msg", msg).apply()
    }

    fun getDays(): Map<String, DayStat> {
        val raw = prefs.getString("days", "{}") ?: "{}"
        val obj = JSONObject(raw)
        val out = LinkedHashMap<String, DayStat>()
        val keys = obj.keys().asSequence().toList().sortedDescending()
        for (k in keys) {
            val d = obj.optJSONObject(k) ?: continue
            out[k] = DayStat(
                date = k,
                arrived = d.optInt("arrived", 0),
                departed = d.optInt("departed", 0),
                updatedAtIso = d.optString("updatedAtIso", ""),
                lastFetchOk = d.optBoolean("lastFetchOk", true),
                errorMsg = d.optString("errorMsg").takeIf { it.isNotBlank() },
                sv = d.optInt("sv", 1)
            )
        }
        return out
    }

    fun saveDay(stat: DayStat) {
        val raw = prefs.getString("days", "{}") ?: "{}"
        val obj = JSONObject(raw)
        val d = JSONObject()
        d.put("arrived", stat.arrived)
        d.put("departed", stat.departed)
        d.put("updatedAtIso", stat.updatedAtIso)
        d.put("lastFetchOk", stat.lastFetchOk)
        d.put("errorMsg", stat.errorMsg ?: "")
        d.put("sv", stat.sv)
        obj.put(stat.date, d)
        prefs.edit().putString("days", obj.toString()).apply()
    }
}","lineStart":1,"lineEnd":76,"totalLines":76,"truncated":false}},"title":"data/data/com.termux/files/home/ruh-counter/app/src/main/java/com/ruh/counter/DayStore.kt","time":{"start":1793498510723,"end":1793498510814}}}

    companion object {
        private const val BASE = "https://airlabs.co/api/v9"
        private const val PAGE = 100
    }

    override fun test(): String {
        val url = "$BASE/schedules?api_key=${enc(key)}&dep_iata=RUH&limit=1"
        val body = httpGet(url, emptyMap(), onCall)
        checkError(body)
        val n = parseData(body).size
        return "AirLabs OK — $n flight(s) sample"
    }

    override fun fetchDay(date: LocalDate): DayFetch {
        val want = TimeFmt.pathDate(date)
        val all = ArrayList<FlightDetail>()
        var raw = 0

        for (q in listOf("dep_iata", "arr_iata")) {
            var offset = 0
            var pages = 0
            while (pages < 20) {
                val url = "$BASE/schedules?api_key=${enc(key)}&$q=RUH" +
                        "&limit=$PAGE&offset=$offset"
                val body = httpGet(url, emptyMap(), onCall)
                checkError(body)
                val items = parseData(body)
                raw += items.size
                for (o in items) {
                    val schedDay = if (q == "arr_iata") {
                        o.optString("arr_time").take(10)
                    } else {
                        o.optString("dep_time").take(10)
                    }
                    if (schedDay != want) continue
                    val d = parseFlight(o, q, date) ?: continue
                    all.add(d)
                }
                val root = JSONObject(body.trim())
                val hasMore = root.optBoolean("has_more", false)
                offset += PAGE
                pages++
                if (!hasMore || items.size < PAGE) break
            }
        }

        val dedup = LinkedHashMap<String, FlightDetail>()
        for (f in all) dedup[f.dir + "/" + f.num] = f
        val list = dedup.values.sortedWith(
            compareBy({ it.dir != "departure" }, { it.sortKey }, { it.num })
        )
        return DayFetch.of(list, raw)
    }

    private fun enc(s: String) = URLEncoder.encode(s, "UTF-8")

    private fun checkError(body: String) {
        val t = body.trim()
        if (t.startsWith("{")) {
            val o = JSONObject(t)
            if (o.has("error")) {
                val e = o.optJSONObject("error")
                throw ApiException(
                    e?.optInt("code") ?: 400,
                    e?.optString("message") ?: t
                )
            }
        }
    }

    private fun parseData(body: String): List<JSONObject> {
        val t = body.trim()
        if (!t.startsWith("{")) return emptyList()
        val root = JSONObject(t)
        val arr = root.optJSONArray("response")
            ?: root.optJSONObject("response")?.optJSONArray("data")
            ?: return emptyList()
        val out = ArrayList<JSONObject>(arr.length())
        for (i in 0 until arr.length()) {
            val o = arr.optJSONObject(i) ?: continue
            out.add(o)
        }
        return out
    }

    private fun parseFlight(o: JSONObject, query: String, date: LocalDate): FlightDetail? {
        val st = o.optString("status").lowercase()
        if (st == "cancelled" || st == "canceled" || st == "diverted") return null

        val dir = if (query == "arr_iata") "arrival" else "departure"
        val depIata = o.optString("dep_iata")
        val arrIata = o.optString("arr_iata")
        if (depIata.isBlank() || arrIata.isBlank()) return null

        val num = o.optString("flight_iata").ifBlank {
            (o.optString("airline_iata") + o.optString("flight_number"))
        }
        if (num.isBlank()) return null

        val airlineName = o.optString("airline_name").ifBlank {
            o.optString("airline_iata")
        }

        val depSched = TimeFmt.hhmm(o.optString("dep_time").ifBlank { o.optString("dep_time_utc") })
        val arrSched = TimeFmt.hhmm(o.optString("arr_time").ifBlank { o.optString("arr_time_utc") })
        val depActual = TimeFmt.hhmm(o.optString("dep_actual").ifBlank { o.optString("dep_actual_utc") })
        val arrActual = TimeFmt.hhmm(o.optString("arr_actual").ifBlank { o.optString("arr_actual_utc") })

        val confirmed = when (dir) {
            "departure" -> depActual != null
            else -> arrActual != null || depActual != null
        }

        val evidence = when {
            confirmed && dir == "departure" -> "real dep $depActual"
            confirmed && depActual != null && arrActual != null -> "dep $depActual · arr $arrActual"
            confirmed && arrActual != null -> "arr $arrActual"
            confirmed && depActual != null -> "dep $depActual"
            else -> "status: ${st.ifBlank { "scheduled only" }}"
        }

        val other = if (dir == "arrival") depIata else arrIata
        val sortSide = if (dir == "departure") depSched else arrSched

        return FlightDetail(
            dir = dir,
            num = num,
            airline = airlineName,
            other = other,
            status = st.ifBlank { "unknown" },
            depReal = depActual,
            arrReal = arrActual,
            depSched = depSched,
            arrSched = arrSched,
            evidence = evidence,
            confirmed = confirmed,
            src = id,
            sortKey = TimeFmt.sortKey(date, sortSide)
        )
    }

                val o = JSONObject(file!!.readText())
                val it = o.keys()
                while (it.hasNext()) {
                    val k = it.next()
                    cache[k] = o.optString(k)
                }
            }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
        }
        loaded = true
    }

    @Synchronized
    fun name(code: String): String? {
        if (code.isBlank()) return null
        val c = code.uppercase()
        BUNDLED[c]?.let { return it }
        return cache[c]?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
    }

    @Synchronized
    fun needsLookup(code: String): Boolean {
        if (code.isBlank()) return false
        val c = code.uppercase()
        if (BUNDLED.containsKey(c)) return false
        return !cache.containsKey(c)
    }

    @Synchronized
    fun put(code: String, name: String) {
        val c = code.uppercase()
        cache[c] = name.trim()
        try {
            val o = JSONObject()
            for ((k, v) in cache) o.put(k, v)
            file?.writeText(o.toString())
        } catch (_: Exception) {

    }

class OpenSkySource(
    private val onCall: ((Map<String, String>) -> Unit)? = null
) : FlightSource {

    override val id = Sources.OPENSKY

    companion object {
        private const val BASE = "https://opensky-network.org/api"
        private const val ICAO = "OERK"
    }

    override fun test(): String {
        val now = java.time.Instant.now().epochSecond
        val url = "$BASE/flights/airport?airport=$ICAO&begin=${now - 3600}&end=$now"
        val body = httpGet(url, emptyMap(), onCall)
        val n = JSONArray(body.trim()).length()
        return "OpenSky OK — $n flight(s) in last hour"
    }

    override fun fetchDay(date: LocalDate): DayFetch {
        val zone = TimeFmt.riyadh
        val start = date.atStartOfDay(zone).toEpochSecond()
        val end = (if (date == TimeFmt.today()) java.time.Instant.now().epochSecond
                   else date.atTime(23, 59).atZone(zone).toEpochSecond())
        if (end <= start) return DayFetch.of(emptyList(), 0)

        val url = "$BASE/flights/airport?airport=$ICAO&begin=$start&end=$end"
        val body = httpGet(url, emptyMap(), onCall)
        val arr = JSONArray(body.trim())
        val flights = ArrayList<FlightDetail>()
        val seen = HashSet<String>()

        for (i in 0 until arr.length()) {
            val o = arr.optJSONObject(i) ?: continue
            val callsign = o.optString("callsign").trim()
            val depAirport = o.optString("estDepartureAirport")
            val arrAirport = o.optString("estArrivalAirport")
            val firstSeen = o.optLong("firstSeen", 0)
            val lastSeen = o.optLong("lastSeen", 0)
            if (firstSeen == 0L) continue

            val num = callsign.ifBlank { "ICAO-${o.optString("icao24")}" }
            val depInstant = if (firstSeen > 0) java.time.Instant.ofEpochSecond(firstSeen) else null
            val arrInstant = if (lastSeen > 0) java.time.Instant.ofEpochSecond(lastSeen) else null
            val depHhmm = depInstant?.atZone(zone)?.format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm"))
            val arrHhmm = arrInstant?.atZone(zone)?.format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm"))

            val dir: String
            val other: String
            val depReal: String?
            val arrReal: String?
            when {
                depAirport == ICAO -> {
                    dir = "departure"
                    other = arrAirport.ifBlank { "" }
                    depReal = depHhmm
                    arrReal = null
                }
                arrAirport == ICAO -> {
                    dir = "arrival"
                    other = depAirport.ifBlank { "" }
                    depReal = null
                    arrReal = arrHhmm
                }
                else -> continue
            }

            val dedupKey = "$dir/$num"
            if (seen.contains(dedupKey)) continue
            seen.add(dedupKey)

            val confirmed = if (dir == "departure") depReal != null else arrReal != null
            val evidence = if (dir == "departure") "ADSB dep $depReal" else "ADSB arr $arrReal"

            flights.add(
                FlightDetail(
                    dir = dir,
                    num = num,
                    airline = "",
                    other = other,
                    status = "seen",
                    depReal = depReal,
                    arrReal = arrReal,
                    depSched = null,
                    arrSched = null,
                    evidence = evidence,
                    confirmed = confirmed,
                    src = id,
                    sortKey = TimeFmt.sortKey(date, depHhmm ?: arrHhmm)
                )
            )
        }

        flights.sortWith(compareBy({ it.dir != "departure" }, { it.sortKey }, { it.num }))
        return DayFetch.of(flights, arr.length())
    }
}

object FlightMerge {
    private fun normNum(num: String): String =
        num.uppercase().replace(Regex("[^A-Z0-9]"), "")

    private fun id(f: FlightDetail): String = f.dir + "/" + normNum(f.num)

    fun merge(newFlights: List<FlightDetail>, oldFlights: List<FlightDetail>): List<FlightDetail> {
        val map = LinkedHashMap<String, FlightDetail>()
        for (f in oldFlights) map[id(f)] = f
        for (f in newFlights) {
            val cur = map[id(f)]
            map[id(f)] = when {
                cur == null -> f
                f.confirmed && !cur.confirmed -> f
                !f.confirmed && cur.confirmed -> cur
                else -> f
            }
        }
        return map.values.sortedWith(
            compareBy({ it.dir != "departure" }, { it.sortKey }, { it.num })
        )
    }

    fun counts(flights: List<FlightDetail>, raw: Int): Counts = Counts(
        flights.count { it.dir == "arrival" && it.confirmed },
        flights.count { it.dir == "departure" && it.confirmed },
        raw
    )
}

Highlights:
The Historical Flight Data API returns historical flight data for already completed flights, so you can run a flight history lookup by flight number and see exactly what happened.

For every past flight you get both the scheduled and the actual departure and arrival times, the flight duration, and the final status - landed, cancelled or diverted - together with departure and arrival delays in minutes.

...

### Historical Flight Data API Request:

```http

                https://airlabs.co/api/v10/historical?flight_iata=AA6&api_key={{params.api_key}}
              
```

### Historical Flight Data API Request Parameters:

| Parameter | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api_key` | required | Your API Key from account dashboard. |
| `flight_iata` | required | Query historical flight data by Flight IATA code-number (e.g. `AA6`). |
| `flight_icao` | required | Query past flight history by Flight ICAO code-number (e.g. `AAL6`). |
| `offset` | optional | Pagination offset for use with result limits (0+ until request.has_more) |

### Historical Flight Data API Response:

```javascript

              [{
                "dep_iata": "HNL",
                "dep_icao": "PHNL",
                "dep_time": "2026-05-05 17:42",
                "dep_actual": "2026-05-05 18:02",
                "arr_iata": "DFW",
                "arr_icao": "KDFW",
                "arr_time": "2026-05-06 06:00",
                "arr_actual": "2026-05-06 05:35",
                "dep_delayed": 20,
                "arr_delayed": null,
                "duration": 438,
                "status": "landed"
              }]
              
```

 The Historical Flight Data API response is shortened for readability and shows the core historical flight data fields. The data may contain errors, and data coverage varies by flight. 

### Historical Flight Data API response parameters:

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dep_iata` | Departure airport IATA code. Available in the Free plan. |
| `dep_icao` | Departure airport ICAO code. |
| `dep_time` | Scheduled departure time in the airport time zone. Available in the Free plan. |
| `dep_actual` | Actual departure time in the airport time zone - when the flight really departed. |
| `arr_iata` | Arrival airport IATA code. Available in the Free plan. |
| `arr_icao` | Arrival airport ICAO code. |
| `arr_time` | Scheduled arrival time in the airport time zone. Available in the Free plan. |
| `arr_actual` | Actual arrival time in the airport time zone - when the flight really landed. |
| `dep_delayed` | Departure delay of the historical flight (in minutes). |
| `arr_delayed` | Arrival delay of the historical flight (in minutes). Can be `null` if not available. |
| `duration` | Total flight time (in minutes). |
| `status` | Historical flight status - `landed`, `cancelled` or `diverted`. |

Highlights:
# eatc-airlines

A command-line tool and API for retrieving scheduled and historical flight data and generating *Endless
ATC* airline configurations.

## Features

- Fetch scheduled and past flights (up to 7 days, or [1 year with a subscription](https://github.com/zefir-git/eatc-airlines/pull/55)) from [AirNav Radar](https://airnavradar.com).
- Convert flight data into `airlines` configuration for *Endless ATC* custom airspace.
- Analyse traffic flow statistics from flight data.
- Simple, fast, and works offline once data is fetched.
- No API key or authentication necessary.

...

### Fetching Flight Data

Retrieve scheduled and historical flights (up to 7 days in the past) for a specific airport.

#### Command:

```sh
eatc-airlines fetch <icao> [path]
```

- ` ` – **ICAO airport code** (e.g., `EGLL` for Heathrow).
- `[path]` – *(Optional)* **File path** to save the data. Defaults to a unique file in the current directory.

#### Example:

```sh
mkdir EGLL && cd EGLL
eatc-airlines fetch EGLL
```

> [!CAUTION]
> Requests might be blocked by Cloudflare. Please see [#52](https://github.com/zefir-git/eatc-airlines/pull/52).

> [!NOTE]
> The fetched JSON files should not be manually edited unless you know what you are doing.

## Glossary:

- "Observed Time Period" (or OTP for short): A period of 7 days, which spans the current day and 3 days before and after the current day. This is the time period that the API returns data for. Historical data is not displayed to unauthenticated (or registered "Standard" plan) users in order to drive subscription sales.

...

No authentication is required for any of these methods at the time of writing.

...

### Airport Arrivals / Departures

GET URL: /api-next/flight-tracker/:type/:airport/:year/:month/:day/:startHour?carrierCode=:code&numHours=:hours

Get arrival/departure information for a certain airport. This endpoint only returns data in the OTP in chunks of a maximum size of 12 hours.

Parameters:

- type: Return arrivals or departures for a certain airport. Must be "arr" or "dep" respectively. Mandatory.
- airport: Must be an IATA 3 letter or an ICAO 4 letter airport code. For example: "SCE". Mandatory.
- year: Year to lookup. Must be year with century. For example: "2022". Mandatory.
- month: Month to lookup. Can be zero-padded or not. For example: "2" or "02". Mandatory.
- day: Day to lookup. Can be zero-padded or not. For example: "3" or "03". Mandatory.
- startHour: The hour at which the lookup starts. Meant to make lookups easier in the web app, as to avoid overwhelming the user with information (for example, the time period 00:00-06:00 would have a startHour of 0). Can be any integer number from 0 to 23. Mandatory.
- carrierCode: Carrier (airline) IATA code. Used for limiting the results to only one airline/carrier. Optional.
- hours: Number of hours to return data for. Can be any integer from 1 to 12. However, the sum of startHour and hours must never exceed 24.

Example URL: https://www.flightstats.com/v2/api-next/flight-tracker/dep/SCE/2022/8/6/0?numHours=12 - Lists departures at SCE airport on

GET URL: /api-next/flight-tracker/other-days/:carrierCode/:number

Get past and upcoming flight information in the OTP for a flight number.

Parameters:

- carrierCode: Carrier (airline) IATA code. Mandatory.
- number: Flight number. Mandatory.

Example URL: https://www.flightstats.com/v2/api-next/flight-tracker/other-days/UA/3867 - Lists all UA 3867 flights in the OTP.

...

## Introduction

The Historical Flight Status APIs give you access to historical flight information, including scheduled, estimated and actual departure/arrival times, equipment type, delay calculations, terminal, gate and baggage carousel. 

Historical Flight Status APIs answer questions such as:

- Was a flight cancelled or diverted?
- Was a flight delayed and by how much?
- What equipment was flown?

Historical Flight Status data is available for flights from February 7, 2006 to present day.

Queries are supported by flight history id; airline, flight number, and date; departure or arrival airport and date; and by route and date.

The categories of Historical Flight Status APIs include:

- By airport - Flights that departed from or arrived at a specific airport on a given date
- By flight - Status for a particular flight
- By route - Flights on a route (departure & arrival airport pair) that departed or arrived on a given date

## Historical Flight Status - Airport Arrivals by Date 

Returns the status of all flights having arrived at an airport within the specified hour, or within a window up to 6 hours wide if numHours is specified.

##### Authorizations:

Authorization

arrivalAirport

required

string

 Example: LAX

Code of the arrival airport. Accepted formats:

- IATA (3-letter)
- ICAO (4-letter)
- FS (3-4 alphanumeric characters, Cirium unique airport code)

All formats are supported and matched in this order: IATA, ICAO, then FS.

arrivalDate

required

 Example: 2015-08-23

Date of arrival in YYYY-MM-DD format (ISO 8601), for example: 2015-10-01.

The date is interpreted in the local time of the arrival airport unless the `utc` flag is set to true.

arrivalHour

string^([0-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-3])$

 Example: 4

Hour of arrival in HH format (0–23), with or without a leading zero. For example: 4 for 4 AM or 16 for 4 PM.

The hour is interpreted in the local time of the arrival airport unless the `utc` flag is set to true.

utc

 Enum: true false 

Possible values are true or false. When true, the arrival or departure date and hour are interpreted in UTC. When false (default), they are interpreted in the local time of the specified airport.

This affects which flights are included in the time window, especially when querying around midnight or across time zones.

numHours

integer [ 1 .. 6 ] 

 Default: 1

 Example: numHours=3

Controls how many hours of arrival or departure flights are returned, starting from the specified hour.

Accepts values from 1 to 6. Default is 1. Used to define the size of the time window.

| Parameter | | Description |

# Historical data

the whole sky, archived every day, free to download.

license: ODbL 1.0, use it freely, just keep it open.

## what is inside

one release = one day of the whole sky, as gzip-compressed JSON written by readsb.

- per aircraft: callsign (`flight`), `hex`, `type`, altitude, `gs`, track,

vertical rate, `squawk`, `category`, `lat`/`lon`.

- per point: signal quality (`nic`, `nac_p`, `sil`, `rc`, `rssi`) and how we

placed it: `adsb`, `mlat` or `tisb`.

- two folders:`traces/` (one file per aircraft, per day) and `heatmap/`

(one small file per day, the replay point cloud).

exact per-record schema: readsb's trace format.

## grab it

the dump runs once a day and lands as a GitHub release, one per instance:

- `readsb-prod-0`
- `readsb-prod-1`
- `readsb-staging-0`

prod is what powers adsb.lol; use it, and fall back to staging for a day if prod looks short.

everything is here: https://github.com/adsblol/globe_history

each release is split into `.aa`, `.ab`, ... parts. join the parts and untar:

```
mkdir 2025.05.18
cat v2025.05.18-planes-readsb-prod-0.tar.aa v2025.05.18-planes-readsb-prod-0.tar.ab | tar -xf - -C 2025.05.18
```

## use it

point your tooling straight at the releases, or clone `globe_history` and let it fetch and index the data for you. build something with it.

This is the source code for the adsb.lol API.

It runs in Kubernetes and is written in Python / asyncio / aiohttp.

This API is compatible with the ADSBExchange Rapid API. It is a drop-in replacement.

## Documentation

Interactive documentation for the API lives at api.adsb.lol/docs

## Rate limits

Rate limits are dynamic based on the environment load.

If you get 4xx errors, you are doing something wrong.

In the future, you will require an API key which you can obtain by feeding adsb.lol.

This will be a way to ensure that the API is being used responsibly and by people who are willing to contribute to the project.

# adsblol/globe_history_2026 (1952 GiB)

This database is made available under the Open Database License: http://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1.0/.

## What is it?

This database is a collection of all the data known to ADSB.lol, uploaded daily.

This includes data from ADSB.lol feeders and friends, FlyItalyADSB and TheAirTraffic.com

## Releases

All files are downloadable from the releases tab of this repository.

See RELEASES.md for a formatted list of links.

Each release is 1 day of flight data.
Download both files from the prod or staging release for a day you're interested in.
(if prod or staging for that day is significantly smaller, ignore it)

The data is added to a tar archive and then the file is split.
To extract the data, adapt the following commands for the files you downloaded:
```
mkdir 2025.05.18
cat v2025.05.18-planes-readsb-prod-0.tar.aa v2025.05.18-planes-readsb-prod-0.tar.ab | tar -xf - -C 2025.05.18
```

## Technically

A dump of the /var/globe_history directory from adsb.lol planes containers.

***Documentation for the format of the files can be found at wiedehopf's readsb***

The planes containers serve adsb.lol. Prod is used, unless it is down then staging is used. There are two replicas of prod and one of staging.

The files in the heatmap directory are used for the the replay functionality.
The files in the traces folder are used when displaying the historic data for a specific aircraft.

The files are written by readsb and are stored in gzip compressed json format.

Historical ADS-B flight trajectory search. Every flight is a full 4D trajectory
(position + altitude + time, plus track, ground speed, vertical rate, IAS and
squawk as time series), ingested from the adsb.lol global archive.

This file is the complete guide to the HTTP API. If you read only this, you can
write correct queries. Machine-readable schema: <https://adsb.aero/api/openapi.json>
(56 KB — you probably don't need it). Human docs: <https://adsb.aero/api/docs>.

- **Base URL**: `https://adsb.aero/api/v1`
- **Auth**: none. Public read-only data.
- **Content type**: `application/json`. CORS is open to all origins.
- **Be polite**: this runs on one box. Prefer one broad query over many narrow
  ones, keep `limit` modest, and don't poll in a loop.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/query` | Search flights. The main endpoint. |
| GET | `/airports/{code}` | **Resolve an ICAO/IATA code to a position _and_ its aerodrome airspace polygons.** |
| GET | `/waypoints/search?q=` | Typeahead over airports, navaids, VFR reporting points, airspaces. |
| GET | `/waypoints/{id}` | One waypoint by OpenAIP ID. |
| GET | `/airspaces?pos=lat,lng&dist=` | Airspaces near a point (`dist` in km, max 100). |
| GET | `/flights/{flight_id}` | Full trajectory for one flight. |
| GET | `/data-range` | `first_date` / `last_date` actually held. Check this before assuming coverage. |
| GET | `/icao-types?start=&end=` | Aircraft types seen in a date range, with counts. |
| GET | `/health` | Liveness. |

## Start here: departures and arrivals

This is the most common question ("who flew into X?", "where do people arriving
at X come from?"), and the way to get it right is not obvious.

There is **no `departs_from`/`arrives_at` predicate and no airport-code filter.**
Endpoints are expressed geometrically: a flight arrived at X if its last position
falls inside a geometry around X.

**Use the aerodrome's published airspace, not a radius.** `GET /airports/{code}`
returns the ATZ / MATZ / CTR polygons whose boundary contains the field. That
boundary is the real, correctly-sized, correctly-shaped extent of the aerodrome —
a guessed radius is too big for a grass strip and too small for a major hub, and
it is circular when real airspace usually isn't.

Step 1 — resolve the code:

```bash
curl https://adsb.aero/api/v1/airports/EGHP
```

```jsonc
{
  "ident": "EGHP", "name": "POPHAM", "lon": -1.2347, "lat": 51.1936,
  "elevation_ft": 550,
  "airspaces": [                      // most specific (smallest) first
    {
      "name": "POPHAM ATZ", "type_name": "ATZ", "area_km2": 7.1,
      "lower_limit": {"value": 0,    "unit": "ft", "ref": "gnd"},
      "upper_limit": {"value": 2550, "unit": "ft", "ref": "msl"},
      "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[...]]]}
    }
  ]
}
```

Step 2 — paste `airspaces[0].geometry` straight into the query:

```bash
curl -X POST https://adsb.aero/api/v1/query \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "match": {
      "endpoint_within": {
        "mode": "end",
        "geometry": { "type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[...]]] }
      }
    },
    "end_date": "2026-09-12T00:00:00Z",
    "window_days": 7,
    "limit": 100,
    "include_path": false
  }'
```

Use `"mode": "start"` for departures, `"end"` for arrivals, `"both"` for
circuits and local flights that began and ended at the same field.

If `airspaces` is empty (many unlicensed strips have no published airspace),
*then* fall back to a circle — 2–3 km for a small field, 8–10 km for a hub:

```json
{"type": "Circle", "coordinates": [-1.2347, 51.1936], "radius": 3000}
```

For a place that is not an airport, use `/waypoints/search?q=...` to get `lon`/`lat`.
Never invent coordinates — look them up.

## POST /query

Request fields:

| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `match` | `null` | Predicate tree. `null` matches everything. |
| `end_date` | newest flight in the archive | Optional. **Exclusive** upper bound on `start_ts`. Omit it to search the most recent data. |
| `window_days` | `7` | Window size in days back from `end_date`. **Max 7.** |
| `start_from` | `null` | Optional floor on `start_ts`. Must be before `end_date`. |
| `limit` | `100` | 1–10000 per page. |
| `cursor` | `null` | From the previous response. |
| `include_path` | `true` | **Set `false` unless you are drawing the trajectory.** |

Response: `{"flights": [...], "cursor": ..., "window_from": ...}`.

Each flight carries `flight_id`, `icao24`, `callsign`, `icao_type`,
`emitter_category`, `registration`, `model`, `year`, `operator`, `start_ts`,
`end_ts`, `start_point`, `end_point`, and `start_airport_ident` /
`end_airport_ident` (+ `_name`) matched at ingest. With `include_path: true` you
also get `path`, `timestamps`, `path_tracks`, `path_gs`, `path_vr`, `path_ias`,
`squawk_runs`, `alt_correction_ft` and `path_agl_ft` — all nine come back `null`
when `include_path` is `false`.

Note the asymmetry: airport idents come back **in results**, but you cannot
*filter* on them — filtering is geometric, as above.

### How the trajectory fields are encoded

There are two shapes here, and they are **not** parallel arrays. Unpacking them
as if they were is the easiest way to get silently wrong numbers.

`path` is a GeoJSON **MultiLineString**: `coordinates` is a list of *segments*,
one per contiguous run of ADS-B coverage (gaps >60 s start a new segment), each
segment a list of `[lon, lat, pressure_alt_ft]`. `timestamps` mirrors it exactly:
`timestamps[i][j]` is the time of `path.coordinates[i][j]`.

Every other series — `path_tracks`, `path_gs`, `path_vr`, `path_ias`,
`path_agl_ft`, `alt_correction_ft`, `squawk_runs` — is a list of segments whose
entries are **`[unix_epoch_seconds, value]` pairs recorded only where the value
changed**. Each is simplified independently, so a segment here will *not* have
the same length as the matching segment of `path.coordinates`. To read a value
at some instant, take the last entry at or before it (forward-fill).

```jsonc
{
  "path":       {"type": "MultiLineString",
                 "coordinates": [[[-0.12, 51.51, 35000.0], [-1.20, 52.50, 36000.0]]]},
  "timestamps": [[1743501600.0, 1743505200.0]],       // parallel to coordinates
  "path_gs":    [[[1743501600.0, 450]]]               // sparse: one change point
}
```

So: to plot altitude against time use `path` + `timestamps`; to plot ground
speed, treat `path_gs` as its own step-function series on its own timestamps.

## Predicates

A predicate is a JSON object with exactly one key. These are all of them:

### Spatial

**`trajectory_intersects`** — the path enters the geometry at any point.
**`trajectory_within`** — the path never leaves the geometry.

Both take the same value object:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `geometry` | GeoJSON `Point`/`LineString`/`Polygon`/`MultiPolygon`/`GeometryCollection`, or `Circle`. |
| `altitude_min` / `altitude_max` | With `altitude_min_ref`/`altitude_max_ref`: `"ft"` (QNH-corrected feet MSL, default) or `"fl"` (flight level, pressure altitude). |
| `agl_min_ft` / `agl_max_ft` | Height above terrain. Good for "low flying". |
| `time_from` / `time_to` | ISO-8601 UTC bounds on time spent inside. |
| `squawk_codes` | Array of squawk strings, e.g. `["7000"]`. |
| `dwell_min_s` / `dwell_max_s` | Seconds spent satisfying every other field in the block. |
| `distance_min_m` / `distance_max_m` | Ground distance (m) covered while satisfying every other field in the block. |

Altitude, time and dwell are evaluated **simultaneously**: `dwell_min_s: 600`
with `altitude_max: 5000` means ten minutes spent inside the geometry *while
below 5000 ft*, not ten minutes inside and separately some time below.

**`geometry` is optional**, and so is everything else: dwell and distance measure
whatever part of the flight the other fields select. Without a geometry,
`trajectory_intersects` with `altitude_min_ref: "fl", altitude_min: 300,
dwell_min_s: 1800` is "at least 30 minutes at or above FL300", and a
`trajectory_within` holding only `distance_min_m` is the flight's whole track
length — **this is how to ask for long or short flights by distance.** For
duration, `{"duration": {...}}` below is the simpler spelling of the same
whole-flight number.

Coverage gaps are bridged: when the aircraft went unobserved, dwell and distance
assume a straight line between the last point before the gap and the first
after it, so an hour-long gap mid-flight still counts as an hour. That is an
estimate — holds or detours flown inside a gap are not seen — but the
alternative, counting only observed stretches, under-reports every flight with
patchy coverage. The `path` returned still shows the gaps.

**There is a cap on how large `geometry` can be.** These two predicates are
accelerated by a spatial index that holds at most 1000 cells per geometry —
about the area of the UK, or a 10°×12° box. Go over it and the query is refused
with a 422 naming the cell count; split the area into tiles, query each, and
merge the results. `endpoint_within` is exempt: it tests a single point per
flight, so any size of geometry is fine there.

**`endpoint_within`** — constrains the departure and/or arrival point.

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `mode` | `"start"`, `"end"`, `"either"` (start OR end), `"both"` (start AND end). Required. |
| `geometry` | As above. |
| `start_time_from` / `start_time_to` | Bounds on `start_ts`. Applied for `start`/`either`/`both`. |
| `end_time_from` / `end_time_to` | Bounds on `end_ts`. Applied for `end`/`either`/`both`. |

### Attribute

| Predicate | Value | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `icao_type` | array of ICAO type designators | `{"icao_type": ["DA40", "C172"]}` |
| `emitter_category` | array of ADS-B categories `A1`–`A7`, `B1`–`B7`, `C1`–`C3` | `{"emitter_category": ["A1"]}` |
| `callsign_prefix` | string prefix (**not** a regex) | `{"callsign_prefix": "BAW"}` |
| `registration_prefix` | string prefix | `{"registration_prefix": "G-AB"}` |
| `icao24` | array of 6-hex Mode S addresses | `{"icao24": ["4ca7b3"]}` |
| `duration` | `{"min_s": ..., "max_s": ...}` — first to last position, gaps included | `{"duration": {"max_s": 3600}}` |

Emitter categories worth knowing: `A1` light, `A2` small, `A3` large,
`A5` heavy, `A7` rotorcraft, `B1` glider, `B2` balloon, `B4` ultralight,
`B6` UAV.

### Boolean

`{"and": [...]}`, `{"or": [...]}`, `{"not": {...}}` — nest freely.

## Worked examples

**Light aircraft that landed at Popham, low and slow.** Resolve `EGHP` first
(above), then:

```json

  "match": {"and": [
    {"endpoint_within": {"mode": "end", "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[...]]]}}},
    {"emitter_category": ["A1"]}
  ]},
  "limit": 200, "include_path": false
}
```

**Where do arrivals at Popham come from?** Query as above, then read
`start_airport_ident` / `start_point` off each result.

    }}
  ]},
  "limit": 100, "include_path": false

```

## Pagination and time windows

One response searches at most `window_days` (max 7) of history. `cursor` hides
that from you: it continues *both* within a window and across window boundaries.

**Page until `cursor` is `null`.** Repeat the identical request with
`"cursor": <the value from the last response>`. When a window runs out the next
cursor moves to the preceding window automatically, so the same loop walks
backwards through time. You do not need to do date arithmetic, and you do not
need to feed `window_from` back as `end_date`.

`cursor` is `null` only when there is nothing further back to read: either the
walk reached the archive's earliest flight, or it reached the `start_from` you
set.

That makes the loop terminating but potentially **long** — with no `start_from`
it will page all the way back to the start of the archive (see `/data-range`;
currently early 2025). So:

- **Set `start_from`** to the earliest date you actually care about. It is the
  only thing that stops the walk early, and it is much cheaper than discarding
  pages you did not want.
- Or stop the loop yourself after enough results, and say what period you
  covered. Each response's `window_from` is the floor of the window it came
  from, which is exactly how far back you have read.

## Gotchas

- **`window_days` maxes out at 7**, so one response covers at most a week.
  Paging on `cursor` walks further back on its own, but if you stop after a
  page or two, report the period you actually covered rather than a week's
  results as if they were a year's.
- **`include_path: false`** unless you are plotting. A trajectory is thousands
  of coordinates; `{"limit": 1000}` with paths is a very large response. It
  nulls every time series, `path_agl_ft` and `alt_correction_ft` included.
- **`end_date` is exclusive** and bounds `start_ts` (departure time), not
  `end_ts`. A flight that departs 23:50 and lands 00:30 belongs to the earlier day.
- **`callsign_prefix` is a prefix, not a regex.** Callsigns are ICAO format
  (`BAW123`), not IATA (`BA123`).
- **Callsign ≠ registration.** `registration_prefix` matches an airframe's
  registration; flights with no linked airframe record never match it.
- **Identifier matching is forgiving, so don't pre-format.** `callsign_prefix`,
  `registration_prefix`, `icao_type` and `emitter_category` are all matched
  case-insensitively with hyphens ignored on both sides, so `g-abcd`, `GABCD`
  and `gAbCd` all match an aircraft registered `G-ABCD` — which matters because
  registrations are *published* with a hyphen and *broadcast* without one.
  `icao24` is lower-cased for you. Pass the identifier however the user said it.
- **`flight_id` is `icao24:start_ts_utc`** — e.g. `4ca7b3:2025-04-15T14:32:18Z`.
- **Altitude reference matters.** `"ft"` is QNH-corrected MSL; flights lacking
  correction data fall back to pressure altitude (±300 ft). `"fl"` is always
  pressure altitude. Use `"fl"` above the transition altitude, `"ft"` below.
- **Coverage is uneven rather than regional.** It is strong over Europe and
  North America — major-airport arrivals are usually tracked down to a few
  hundred feet — and thins out over oceans, and at low level away from populated
  areas. Call `/data-range` for the dates held. An empty result may mean no
  coverage, not no flights.
- **`operator` is the airframe's registered owner, not the airline.** It comes
  from the registry, so an airliner frequently reads as a bank or leasing trust
  (`WILMINGTON TRUST CO TR` for a US carrier's 787). Use the `callsign` prefix —
  the ICAO airline code, e.g. `BAW` — if you want the operating carrier.
- **Ground data is excluded.** Trajectories are airborne points only, so taxi
  and ground movement do not appear.
- **A 422 response includes a `hint` field** telling you what was wrong. Read it.

## Terms

Data derives from the [adsb.lol](https://adsb.lol) archive (ODbL), with
reference data from [OpenAIP](https://openaip.net). Positions are crowd-sourced
receiver data: coverage is uneven, low-level and remote flights are often
missing, and not all aircraft transmit ADS-B. Treat absence as absence of
evidence. Do not present this as a complete or authoritative record of flights.

    cs = (cs or "").strip().upper()
    for n in (3, 2):
        code = cs[:n]
        if code in AIRLINE_NAMES:
            return code, AIRLINE_NAMES[code]
    return cs[:3] if len(cs) >= 3 else cs, ""

def fetch_json(url, payload=None, retries=5):
    for attempt in range(retries):
        try:
            if payload is None:
                r = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
            else:
                r = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=120)
            if r.status_code in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504):
                time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
                continue
            r.raise_for_status()
            return r.json()
        except Exception:
            if attempt == retries - 1:
                raise
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
    raise RuntimeError("request failed")

object DataReset {
    private const val VERSION = 4

        if (prefs.getInt("data_reset_v", 0) >= VERSION) return

        seedFromAsset(context)

    }

    private fun seedFromAsset(context: Context) {

        val lines = reader.readLines()
        reader.close()

        val header = lines.first().split(",")
        fun idx(name: String): Int = header.indexOf(name)

            if (line.isBlank()) continue
            val c = line.split(",")
            val date = c[idx("flight_date_sa")]
            if (date.isBlank()) continue
            val d = LocalDate.parse(date)
            val dir = c[idx("direction")]
            val num = c[idx("callsign")]
            if (num.isBlank()) continue
            val airline = c[idx("airline")]
            val other = if (dir == "arrival") c[idx("origin_iata_or_icao")] else c[idx("destination_iata_or_icao")]
            val depReal = TimeFmt.hhmm(c[idx("observed_takeoff_sa")])
            val arrReal = TimeFmt.hhmm(c[idx("observed_landing_sa")])
            val conf = c[idx("confidence")].ifBlank { "medium" }
            val missing = c[idx("missing_fields")]
            val evidence = "adsb.aero observed endpoints (confidence: $conf; missing: $missing)"
            val sortSide = if (dir == "departure") (depReal ?: "00:00") else (arrReal ?: "00:00")
            val flight = FlightDetail(
                dir = dir,
                num = num,
                airline = airline,
                other = other,
                status = "observed",
                depReal = depReal,
                arrReal = arrReal,
                depSched = null,
                arrSched = null,
                evidence = evidence,
                confirmed = true,
                src = "adsb.aero",
                confidence = conf,
                sortKey = TimeFmt.sortKey(d, sortSide)
            )
            byDate.getOrPut(date) { ArrayList() }.add(flight)
        }

        val dayStore = DayStore(context)
        val flightStore = FlightStore(context)
        for ((date, flights) in byDate) {
            flightStore.save(date, flights)
            val counts = FlightMerge.counts(flights, flights.size)
            dayStore.saveDay(
                DayStat(
                    date = date,
                    arrived = counts.arrived,
                    departed = counts.departed,
                    updatedAtIso = Instant.now().toString(),
                    lastFetchOk = true,
                    errorMsg = null,
                    sv = SCHEMA_V
                )
            )
        }
    }
}
